common.rows: Main set of addendum l: 1,258,807 scored work-format-months, origins 2019-01 to 2026-07, rows of data/db/wiki_led/l_books_in_time/rows.parquet, test years 2019 to 2026; checked against l_books_in_time/preds.parquet.
common.base_models: HM (library history and calendar month) and HMW14 (HM plus the book's own and author's pages), stored five-seed predictions of l07 (seed 20261020 equals l04).
common.time_rule: Every feature at origin t uses only data dated on or before the last day of month t (weeks that ended by then; list weeks published by then; reviews and reading-log entries dated by then).
common.placebo_dates: For every new signal X, X_lag: the row's X features at origin t replaced by the same book's X features at origin t-12 (dates moved 12 months later, so no later data is used), as in addendum m.
common.seeds_and_intervals: LightGBM seeds 20261020 to 20261024; each value the five-seed mean; 2,000 draws of 3-month blocks (seed 20261020, the draws of l04) with the five-seed mean recomputed in each draw; one-sided p = (1 + draws at or below 0) / 2,001.
common.segments: Each primary gain is split by the 14 families of addendum m (B_segments) with the same group definitions, scoring, group-minus-rest, Benjamini-Hochberg at 0.05 within each comparison, too-small rule and wording rule.
common.outputs: Code code/main_study/wiki_led/n_more_signals/; data data/db/wiki_led/n_more_signals/; plain-language report data/reports/more_signals_single_books.md and tables; published in a pull request after the results, as addendum m.

part_1_signals_in_hand.N_bestseller_lists: New York Times lists from the stored collection (data/db/wiki_led/dirs/d3_nyt/nyt_entries.parquet, June 2008 to October 2026; non-series lists as in code/main_study/wiki_led/dirs/d3_nyt.py). Matching extended from the well-known books to the main set with d3_nyt.py's rules unchanged (ISBN route: the list's ISBN against the Seattle records' ISBNs and the Wikidata edition ISBNs of the work's matched book item, with the title check; else the title and author route with D3's tightened rules). An independent check of 50 random matched main-set works (Seattle title and creator beside the list title and author) is reported; if more than 5 of 50 are wrong, the rule that produced them is tightened and logged before any model. Features at t: n_on (on any list in a week published in month t), n_enter (on a list in t and not in t-1), n_weeks (weeks on lists in t), n_weeks3 (weeks on lists in t-2 to t), n_ever (log of 1 + weeks on lists before t). Unmatched works: 0 (a matched-book flag n_matched is added).
part_1_signals_in_hand.AD_film_and_TV_pages: The English Wikipedia articles of the film and TV adaptations of each work's matched book item (the adaptation items and the film/TV class walk of addendum m's m01; English article from the item's enwiki sitelink). Daily user views 2015-07-01 to 2026-09-30 (Wikimedia per-article service, at most 3 requests a second, one downloader at a time; pages already stored are reused). Per work, the weekly share of all English views summed over its adaptation articles; features at t: the 7 article features of addendum l (article_features() of l02_views.py, unchanged), ad_out (an adaptation released on or before t by addendum m's release rule) and ad_since (months since the latest such release, capped at 120). Missing for works with no such article.
part_1_signals_in_hand.LK_linked_pages: Pages linked to the work's matched book item through Wikidata, by addendum j's link rules (code/main_study/wiki_led/dirs/j1_links.py, J2 to J4: main subject or depicts, set in period, narrative location, characters; the book's own item, its authors, adaptations and series left out), read from best-rank (truthy) statements of the item claims fetched by wbgetentities (batches of 10, at most 3 requests a second); linked items' English articles from their enwiki sitelinks. Views as AD (stores of j1, Test F, study2r reused). Per work, the weekly share summed over its linked articles; features at t: the 7 article features plus lk_pages (log of 1 + linked articles with views by t). Missing for works with none.
part_1_signals_in_hand.OL_reading_intent: Open Library reading-log entries (the dump of addendum k, data/raw/openlibrary_dump/ol_dump_reading-log_2026-09-30.txt.gz, read with python -I and k1_intent.py's strict line pattern). Works mapped through the Open Library work id (P648) on the matched book item's claims (no search; works without it are unmapped). Features at t as k1 (K5): entries in month t on Want to Read, Currently Reading, Already Read and all three; want-to-read in t against the median of t-6 to t-1 (1 added to both, log); entries in t-2 to t. Months 2017-01 to 2026-09. Known limit (as k): the dump holds only entries still on a shelf on 2026-09-30.
part_1_signals_in_hand.models: For each X in {N, AD, LK, OL}: HMW14X (primary), X alone (X plus fmt), HMW14X_lag (placebo). Also HMW14_ALL (HMW14 plus N, AD, LK and OL together) and ALL_lag.
part_1_signals_in_hand.decisions: Signal X passes when (1) HMW14X minus HMW14 change rank has a one-sided p that passes Holm's correction at 0.05 over the five signals of parts 1 and 2 (N, AD, LK, OL, AZ) with an estimate above 0, and (2) HMW14X minus HMW14X_lag has a 95% interval above 0. Secondary, with intervals: X alone; HMW14_ALL minus HMW14 and minus ALL_lag; the top-20 lists and the early-warning list; by format; 2024 to 2026. Segments: the gain HMW14X minus HMW14 for every X, and HMW14_ALL minus HMW14, by the 14 families.

part_2_amazon_reviews.source: Amazon Reviews 2023 (McAuley Lab, UC San Diego; released for research): benchmark/0core/rating_only/Books.csv.gz (602 MB: user id, item parent_asin, rating, time) and raw/meta_categories/meta_Books.jsonl.gz (4.9 GB: item title, author, details with ISBNs), from https://mcauleylab.ucsd.edu/public_datasets/data/amazon_2023/. Both are streamed and reduced while downloading: user ids are never written to disk; the ratings become counts and rating sums per item and month; the metadata keeps only item id, title, author name, ISBN-10, ISBN-13 and publication date. Read as untrusted data (python -I, scripts outside the data folder).
part_2_amazon_reviews.matching: Seattle main-set works to Amazon items: (a) ISBN: the Seattle records' ISBNs and the Wikidata edition ISBNs of the matched book item against the item's ISBN-10 or ISBN-13; (b) else title and author: the normalized main title (text before ':' or '(' , leading article removed, letters and digits only) equal on both sides and the Seattle creator's family name a word of the Amazon author name. A work gets the sum over all its matched items (editions). An independent check of 50 random matched works is reported; if more than 5 of 50 are wrong, the title route is tightened and logged before any model.
part_2_amazon_reviews.months: Reviews are dated by their time stamp (UTC month). The last usable month is the last month whose total number of reviews is at least half of the median of the 12 months before it; later months are missing. Features at t: az_n (log of 1 + reviews in t), az_r (log of (1 + reviews in t) over (1 + median of t-6 to t-1)), az_3 (log of 1 + reviews in t-2 to t), az_cum (log of 1 + reviews up to t), az_rating (mean rating over t-11 to t, missing without reviews); missing for unmatched works and after the last usable month.
part_2_amazon_reviews.models_and_decision: HMW14AZ, AZ alone, HMW14AZ_lag; scored only on rows whose origin month is on or before the last usable month (target years 2019 on). Decision as part 1 (Holm over the five signals, and beating the moved dates). Segments as part 1.
part_2_amazon_reviews.budget: About 5.5 GB downloaded, within the 15 GB allowed without asking; no cloud spend.

part_3_models.3a_book_against_author: Does the book's own page or the author's page carry the gain? HMB = HM plus the 7 book-article features; HMA = HM plus the 7 author-article features. Placebos: HMB_donor, the book features of another main-set work's book article with the closest median lvl4 over origins 2016-03 to 2018-12 (different creator, each donor article at most 3 times, order drawn with seed 20261125); HMA_donor, the same for author articles (different author article). Decisions: the book page adds when HMB minus HM passes Holm over the two pages (one-sided, 0.05) with an estimate above 0 and HMB minus HMB_donor has a 95% interval above 0; the same for the author page. Descriptive: HMW14 minus HMB (author beyond book) and HMW14 minus HMA (book beyond author); by format; by the family 'own Wikipedia article'.
part_3_models.3b_models_per_kind_of_book: For the families F3 popularity, F4 fiction or nonfiction, F6 format and F9 own Wikipedia article (groups as addendum m; for training rows the group is taken the same way at the row's own origin, popularity thirds from the row's own test year), HM and HMW14 are fitted separately within each group (training rows of that group only), five seeds. Reported with intervals for every group: per-group model minus the pooled model on the group's rows (HM and HMW14), and the own-page gain under per-group models minus under the pooled model. Benjamini-Hochberg at 0.05 within each of these three comparisons. No pass rule.
part_3_models.3c_transformer: Chronos-2 (amazon/chronos-2, revision 29ec3766d36d6f73f0696f85560a422f50e8498c, the version of the theme benchmark; pretrained, used without training, on the CPU) forecasts each row's next month from the series' monthly log(1 + loans) over up to 60 months ending at t (excluded months and months before the first loan missing): C2 without covariates; C2W with the monthly log share of views of the book's own and author's articles as past covariates (missing where no article). Median forecast; predicted change = median minus log(1 + M6). Chronos-2 has no random part, so it has no seeds. Reported: C2 and C2W change ranks against HM and HMW14 (paired differences with intervals); C2W minus C2 (what the pages add to the Transformer). Stacking: HMW14Z (HMW14 plus the C2 and C2W predictions as two features), five seeds, against HMW14. Speed rule fixed now: if the time measured on the first 10,000 rows implies more than 24 hours for all 1,773,531 rows of one setting, only the scored rows (origins 2019-01 on) are forecast and stacking is dropped; written in DEVIATIONS before any score.

order_of_work: 1 this record, fingerprinted and public before any step; 2 part 3a (no new data); 3 data for part 1 and part 2 (matches, checks, downloads, features; data reports with counts only); 4 models for parts 1, 2 and 3b; 5 Chronos-2 for part 3c (background, longest); 6 scoring and report; 7 code and results in a pull request. known_limits: Wikidata-based signals (AD, LK, OL) exist only for works with a matched book item, mostly well-known books; which works have one uses Wikidata as of October 2026.
